why: Without the generalised branch every group clones the first group's header row (Artists'), misaligning Places, Recordings, URLs, … — the default for multi-table pages.

why: The table's data-mb-col-headers never reaches group.colHeaders, so the render falls back to the shared header.

why: The reloaded page holds the native relationship lists again; they would stay beside the restored tables.

why: "One table for all relationships" must give a single table with Type and From.

why: With the setting off, the series' own relationships stay native.

name: native series section: its h3 stays an h3
why: renderGroupedTable()'s initial cleanup removes every h3 in #content, so the series name would vanish from the section left native.

name: '#' is not an integer column
why: The declaration gives '#' its right-aligned, tabular-figure cells. Numeric SORTING does not depend on it: _sortColumnKind()'s name heuristic already treats any header containing '#' as numeric.

edits.find:
eventDetailsToTables: true,
                groupByH3: true,
                integerColumns: [ { sourceColumn: '#', align: 'R' } ]
